blocks.text: OPINI - it is important that we in democracy to know the facts and phenomena that occur in the development of democratic life in Indonesia which are still occupied by oligarchs who have power and power from the time of the New Order to the post-reformation.
They're what we often call oligarchs. Oligarki is a ghost to the order of our democracy.
Hadiz and Robison (2004) wrote an oligarki theme in order to explain the Indonesian political phenomenon pasca- Soeharto.
The oligarchs' theory is used to describe the forces that have become a circle of power in Indonesia. They dominate the economic structure and political structures of Indonesia's pasca- New Order.
Conceptually, Oligarki's term has long been known in political studies. This term stretches from ancient Greece to the present contemporary era.

In International Encyclopedia of Social Sciences, Oligarki is defined as a government form where power is in the hands of a small minority. The term is taken from the Greek word, Ez Oligarchia Hikmah, which means government by little, comprised of the word oligoi, and arkhein.

In Jeffrey A Winters' book, with the title of Espagarchy Estates, which he wrote as a reflection attempt to uncover what and actually oligarchs and their role in democratic countries. According to Winters (2011), Oligarki was the one who used wealth to defend his power. It's always been an individual, not an institution or an agency.

On the other hand, Winters felt it was very important to put the oligarchs term in two dimensions as an understanding. The first dimension, Oligarki had a power base for material wealth that was very difficult to break down and balance. Secondly, Oligarki has a vast and systemic reach, despite his minority position in the community.

It also explained that Winters was so excited about the democratic realities in Indonesia that Indonesian democracy was ruled by oligarchs that it was further and further away from the idea of researching people. That, Winters said, was seen as it grew deeper and deeper between the rich and the poor in Indonesia. So, in Indonesia, the rich get richer and poorer get poorer.
Concentrate on wealth and inequality.
When Indonesian democracy was consolidated, oligarchs established a major position in Indonesia's political life. Their grip on Indonesian politics seemed very clear, structured and systematic.

It means that the Indonesian oligarchs are most accurately described as the electronic collective ruler. Or, in other words, a connected oligarch with the government and the collective power of the Electoral. It's also experienced by other countries in the world, of course with different differences and equations.

In his other writing of Eka Oligarki and Democracy published by Prism magazine, Winters has traced the political change in his wealth defense since the Soekarno era, the New Order of Soeharto, to this day.

According to writers who are assessing the impact of oligarchs in Indonesian politics, extreme wealth inequality between citizens is constantly leading to extreme political inequality as well as extremes.

On the other hand, his power in Indonesia can be dominant and distorting, as well as not supplying him with legal infrastructure because of the weakness of organizing and mobilization between civil society actors.

That according to the data of all the political resources in Indonesia, material power is clearly the most concentrated, versatile, durable, and less limited. The power of material in Indonesian society is one of the largest in the world.

The 2010 data shows that the average net worth of forty oligarchs in Indonesia is more than 630,000 times GDP per capita Indonesia (in Thailand and South Korea). Even though the oligarchs are less than 2 / 1 million, their combined assets are equal to 10 percent GDP.

Even if we expand the observation lens to cover 43,000 Indonesians with a smooth financial asset of about 1 million dollars in assets, the result still shows the concentration of material power resources very large remains in the hands of a handful of people.

In the name of the people
Everything that has to do with political life and democracy should be called people. Because politics, as Aristotle and Plato think, are a means of achieving the best political society.
Whereas democracy is as pure as it is of the people, by the people, and for the people, exactly as Abraham Lincoln's.

Therefore, people must become the full and serious care of various forms of political life and democracy in Indonesia as our constitution, that power is in the hands of the people. Messages of prosperity, prosperity, justice and such must be manifested as a success in state.
